records.description: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.93 so the restart loop uses about 27.9 s of the 30 s CPU budget, leaving all other logic unchanged.

Replace the random-restart loop with basin hopping: after one SLSQP run, repeatedly perturb the best packing with Gaussian noise (sigma 0.02) on centres and radii, re-optimise from that start, and keep the result only if its repaired radius sum improves.

issues: Measurement integrity: nothing found. The diff reads no files, uses no network, has no pasted coordinates and does not touch the harness. All randomness comes from rng seeded by the seed argument.

Correctness: no bugs that would make the result meaningless. Every candidate still goes through clip and _repair, so the returned packing stays valid. Negative radii from the perturbation are clamped to 0. The time check is the same as in the incumbent. Each SLSQP call takes about as long as before, so the risk of going over 45 s is unchanged.

The search is now different: it does basin hopping from a single start instead of independent random restarts. If one 30 s run gets stuck in a poor basin, it cannot get out, so results may vary more between seeds. The sigma of 0.02 is a fixed choice that was not tuned.

Statistics: only 2 candidate runs. Their mean is -2.92935, which is 0.00405 better than the incumbent's -2.9253. With a noise sd of 0.0034, z = 0.00405 / (0.0034 * sqrt(1/2 + 1/10)) ≈ 1.54. That matches the harness value of 1.522 to within rounding. The gain is about one noise sd and rests on n=2, so the evidence is weak. A replicate before treating this as a confirmed improvement would be worth the slot.
The meaning of 'adjusted values' is not stated, so I could not check it. The z above assumes they are plain official losses.

records.description: Replace the random-restart loop with basin hopping: after one SLSQP run, repeatedly perturb the best packing with Gaussian noise (sigma 0.02) on centres and radii, re-optimise from that start, and keep the result only if its repaired radius sum improves.
Widen the initial centre box to the full unit square (INIT_LOW 0.1 -> 0.0) and sample initial radii uniformly in [0.01, 0.1] instead of fixing them at 0.05.
Anneal per-circle radius weights (random start around 1, then halfway to 1) over two weighted SLSQP calls before an unweighted true-sum polish, keeping the repair and best-tracking unchanged.

Seed the basin-hopping run with a two-phase start: first SLSQP with all radii tied to one shared variable t (maximising t under the packing constraints), then the existing SLSQP call with radii released to independent variables.

Anneal the basin-hopping perturbation sigma geometrically from 0.05 to 0.002 over the time budget, accepting moves into a current chain when the repaired radius sum improves while tracking the global best separately.

issues: No integrity concerns: no file or network access, no hardcoded coordinates, all randomness uses the seeded rng, and the time-budget check is equivalent to the incumbent's.

`cur` is updated only on strict improvement, using the same test as `best`, so it always equals `best` and is dead code. The only real change is the noise size, which now anneals from 0.05 to 0.002 instead of staying fixed at 0.02. This is not the simulated annealing the comment suggests.
The two candidate runs differ by 0.0165, about 3.4 times the expected 0.0048 for two runs at noise sd 0.0034. The early large-noise phase may sometimes give a worse result.
Recomputed z = (-2.9293 - (-2.92625)) / (0.0034 * sqrt(1/2 + 1/2)) ≈ -0.90, which matches the reported -0.901. The candidate is about 0.003 worse, so rejecting it is correct.

records.description: Anneal the basin-hopping perturbation sigma geometrically from 0.05 to 0.002 over the time budget, accepting moves into a current chain when the repaired radius sum improves while tracking the global best separately.

Before each SLSQP solve, run a penalty continuation stage: L-BFGS-B minimises the squared overlap and wall penalties minus lambda times the radius sum, with lambda increased geometrically over 5 stages, and its output seeds SLSQP.

Replace the basin-hopping loop with random subset re-optimisation: each step picks the 12 circles nearest a random point, runs SLSQP on only those with the rest frozen as obstacles, and keeps the result if the repaired full radius sum improves.

Replace the random SLSQP start with a Lubachevsky-Stillinger-style growth compression (grow radii, push overlaps apart with vectorised gradient steps, halve the growth rate and jitter when jammed) and feed its jammed packing into the existing SLSQP and basin-hopping stages.
With probability 0.5 each basin-hopping step, start from an (n+1)-circle SLSQP solve with its smallest-radius circle deleted instead of perturbing the incumbent.

Replace the uniform random first-start centres in _solve_once with best-candidate (Mitchell) Poisson-disk sampling (k=30 candidates per point, keeping the one farthest from existing centres), with radii set to half the distance to the nearest centre or wall, leaving basin hopping unchanged.

With probability 0.5 the first SLSQP start uses a mirror-symmetric configuration (about x = 0.5 or the diagonal, with one random circle dropped when n is odd), otherwise the existing uniform start; only the initial solve is affected, since basin hopping takes over afterwards.

Replace the uniform random first-start in _solve_once with a greedy largest-hole sequential placement (circles placed in decreasing random target radius on a 200x200 grid, each at the point maximising clearance to existing circles and walls), used as the SLSQP x0.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The edit reads no files, uses no network, pastes no coordinates and does not touch the harness. All randomness comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The greedy start only changes x0. SLSQP and the existing repair step still produce the final packing, so the validity checks still apply. The cost is small: a 40000x32 distance matrix per placement and 32 placements per start, so it will not come near the 45 s limit.

Recomputed z. Candidate mean loss is -2.9292 and incumbent mean is -2.9293, so the candidate is about 0.0001 worse. With sd 0.0034 and 2 runs on each side, SE = 0.0034*sqrt(1/2+1/2) = 0.0034, so z is about -0.03 (convention: positive means the candidate is better). The incumbent mean is rounded, so the true z is somewhere between about -0.015 and -0.044. The harness value of -0.038 fits this. The difference is pure noise, so rejecting is correct.

Minor: INIT_LOW and INIT_RADIUS may now be unused, so they are dead constants. The greedy start may also give less varied restarts than uniform random centres. Each start's positions depend only on its random targets, which could hurt the multi-start search. Both of these are about quality, not integrity.

records.description: Replace the uniform random first-start in _solve_once with a greedy largest-hole sequential placement (circles placed in decreasing random target radius on a 200x200 grid, each at the point maximising clearance to existing circles and walls), used as the SLSQP x0.

Add a grown start: solve n-1 circles, insert one circle at the largest empty spot among 2000 random candidates with its maximal feasible radius, re-run SLSQP for n circles, and keep it as a candidate incumbent alongside the random start.

Adds a rattler-reinsertion move: with probability 0.3 per basin-hopping step, the smallest rattler (fewer than two active contacts) is moved to the grid point with the largest clearance and SLSQP is re-run from there, instead of the usual Gaussian perturbation.

Adds a rattler-reinsertion move: with probability 0.3 per basin-hopping step, the smallest rattler (fewer than two active contacts) is moved to the grid point with the largest clearance and SLSQP is re-run from there, instead of the usual Gaussian perturbation.
Threshold-accepting basin hopping: keep a separate current solution, accept candidates within a linearly shrinking threshold (0.01 to 0) of it, perturb from it, and track the global best separately.
Threshold-accepting basin hopping: keep a separate current solution, accept candidates within a linearly shrinking threshold (0.01 to 0) of it, perturb from it, and track the global best separately.

Replace the single basin-hopping chain with 4 Metropolis chains at a geometric temperature ladder from 0.0005 to 0.01, each sweep attempting replica-exchange swaps between neighbouring temperatures and returning the best packing seen by any chain, with the time budget and perturbation scale unchanged.

Replace the single basin-hopping chain with 4 Metropolis chains at a geometric temperature ladder from 0.0005 to 0.01, each sweep attempting replica-exchange swaps between neighbouring temperatures and returning the best packing seen by any chain, with the time budget and perturbation scale unchanged.

Before each basin-hopping SLSQP solve, move the smallest-radius circle to the best of 30 random centres, scored by the local sum of radii after setting its radius to the largest non-overlapping value.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff adds no file or network access and pastes no coordinates. All randomness comes from the seeded rng, and the existing repair and clip steps still run after the new step, so the packings stay valid.

Recomputed z: candidate mean -2.9346 against incumbent mean -2.9293 is an improvement of 0.0053. With a per-job sd of 0.0034 and 2 runs on each side, the standard error is sqrt(0.0034²/2 + 0.0034²/2) = 0.0034, so z ≈ 1.56. The harness reports 1.540; the small gap is probably rounding in the incumbent mean. The claim matches the numbers.
The evidence is thin: only 2 runs on each side and z is about 1.5. If the budget allows, one more replicate would make the accept more solid.

The relocation score is an odd heuristic. It adds the radii of nearby circles (within 0.05 of contact) to rk, which steers the moved circle towards crowded areas rather than towards the largest free gap. This is not a bug that makes the result meaningless, but the stated idea of 'local sum of radii' only loosely justifies it.
_relocate runs on every restart and always moves the smallest circle, even if that circle is already well placed. This is a minor cost, not a correctness problem.

records.description: Before each basin-hopping SLSQP solve, move the smallest-radius circle to the best of 30 random centres, scored by the local sum of radii after setting its radius to the largest non-overlapping value.

Build the initial incumbent from two-cluster merges (two half-size SLSQP packings in half-width sub-squares, scaled and joined, then a full SLSQP re-solve), repeated for the first 25% of the time budget, and keep the best before the unchanged basin-hopping loop.

During each basin-hopping SLSQP solve, the objective becomes -sum(w_i * r_i) with per-call weights w_i drawn from uniform[0.9, 1.1] by the seeded rng, while the first unweighted start and the true-sum acceptance rule stay unchanged.

Build the SLSQP pair-constraint list per call from only the pairs whose centre distance is below the sum of the start radii plus 0.15, keeping wall and non-negativity constraints for all circles, with the existing full-pair repair step still validating the final packing.

Adds a local cluster shake to basin hopping: with probability 0.5 each step, five circles (a random circle and its 4 nearest neighbours) are redrawn uniformly in the square with radii halved, otherwise the existing global Gaussian perturbation is used, followed by the same relocation, solve, repair and accept-if-better rule.

Replace the uniform random first-start centres with a ring-shell layout: about 4*sqrt(n) circles evenly spaced on a perimeter inset 0.05 with an rng angular offset, and the rest uniform in [0.15, 0.85]^2, with radii at INIT_RADIUS.

Run SLSQP in two stages inside _solve_once: first with the wall constraints tightened by a 0.02 margin, then again with margin zero starting from that result, so edge circles can grow in the second stage.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. All randomness comes from the seeded rng, and the existing repair step still makes the final packing valid.

z checks out: the gain is 2.9364 - 2.9346 = 0.0018. Its standard error is 0.0034*sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) = 0.00416, so z = 0.43. That is within noise, so 'reject' is the right provisional call. The candidate has only 1 run.

Small flaw, not a veto: in _mc_start every radius grows at the same time against the old radii (d - r[None]), so after a growth step neighbouring disks can overlap a little. Later Monte Carlo moves then check against a packing that is already invalid. This only affects the SLSQP start point, and _repair still makes the final output valid, so the result still means something.

The change only affects the first start. The later random restarts are unchanged. The Monte Carlo loop runs in pure Python (2000 sweeps x 32 disks) and probably takes about a second, which counts against the time budget but is well under 45 s. The diff doesn't show the _solve_once signature, but the job ran without crashing, so it must accept the start argument.
To tell whether the gain is real, it needs more replicate runs or a larger effect. The added code is moderately complex for a gain this small.

records.description: Replace the random SLSQP first start with a hard-disk Monte Carlo compression (2000 sweeps of Gaussian moves and radius growth, step scale decaying by 0.99 every 50 sweeps) whose output seeds SLSQP.

Randomised constraint tightening: each basin-hopping SLSQP solve uses a margin m ~ U[0, 0.003] on all non-overlap and wall constraints, followed by an m=0 SLSQP pass from that result so the returned packing satisfies the true constraints.

Adds a reheated restart: basin hopping keeps a separate chain solution that is replaced by a fresh random SLSQP start after 40 steps without a new global best, while the global best is kept unchanged.

Adds a lattice-perturbed start: with probability 0.5 the first SLSQP solve begins from a jittered square or hexagonal lattice (random orientation near 0 or 30 degrees, random spacing, n points kept inside the square, jitter 0.03, clipped to [0.05, 0.95], radii 0.05), otherwise the existing uniform random start is used.

With probability 0.3 per basin-hopping step, slide a random wall-touching circle along its wall to a uniform random position (radius kept) and solve from there without relocation; otherwise keep the existing perturbation and relocation.

Adds a merge-and-split topology move to basin hopping: with probability 0.2 per step, a random close pair is merged into one circle at its midpoint, and a circle is reinserted at the largest hole found from 500 random samples, before the usual relocate and SLSQP solve.
Pass an exact analytic Jacobian (objective gradient and constraint Jacobian for pair, wall and radius terms, built from the iu index arrays) to SLSQP so it no longer relies on finite differences.

Adds a sub-disk rotation kick to basin hopping: each step, the centres within a random radius R in [0.2, 0.35] of a random point p are rotated about p by a random angle in [-pi/3, pi/3], then clipped to the square before the usual Gaussian perturbation, relocation and SLSQP.

issues: Integrity is fine. The edit only changes the random starting points to a Latin-hypercube layout. It draws all randomness from the seeded rng. There is no file access and no pasted coordinates, and the solver and repair step are untouched.

Possible minor bug: `u` has shape (n, 2), so `ravel()` gives x0,y0,x1,y1,... If `_solve_once` reads x0[:n] as the x values and x0[n:2n] as the y values, the points are not a true Latin hypercube. Each axis would then get a mix of x and y strata. The starting points stay inside [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW] and are still random, so the result is not meaningless, but the intended change may not be what runs. Use `u.T.ravel()` if the layout is xs then ys.

Recomputing z: the gain is -2.9347 - (-2.9346) = -0.0001 in loss, so 0.0001 in sum of radii. The standard error is 0.0034*sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00416, so z ≈ 0.024 from the rounded values. Rounding to 4 decimals lets the true gain be anywhere from 0 to 0.0002, which gives z between 0 and 0.048. The harness's 0.008 fits that range.
There is only one candidate run, and the difference is far below the noise sd of 0.0034. The data give no evidence of an improvement, so rejecting is correct.

records.description: Replace the uniform random initial centres in _solve_once with a Latin hypercube sample over [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, using independently permuted strata for x and y so the SLSQP starts are more evenly spread.

memo: Helped: basin hopping replacing random restarts (slot 1, -2.9313/-2.9274) and relocating the smallest circle before each solve (slot 23, -2.9353/-2.9339; incumbent -2.9346 over 2 runs). Gains are close to the noise sd of 0.0034, so be cautious. Single unconfirmed runs 0.0019 or more better than the incumbent: slot 25 two-cluster merge start (-2.9366), slot 26 weighted objective (-2.9365), slot 30 two-stage wall tightening (-2.9368), slot 31 hard-disk Monte Carlo start (-2.9364). Did not help: longer time fraction (-2.9204), tied-radii start (-2.9225), penalty continuation (-2.9048), subset re-optimisation (-2.8822), symmetric start (-2.9155), pair-list pruning (-1.7220, broke the packing). Init changes, extra moves and heavy restructuring mostly failed or were neutral. Next: replicate slots 25, 26, 30 and 31, then stack the best one or two on the relocation move. Also try small in-loop tweaks such as swapping a small and a large circle. Keep edits small. The gap to the published 2.9370 is about 0.003.

incumbent.description: Before each basin-hopping SLSQP solve, move the smallest-radius circle to the best of 30 random centres, scored by the local sum of radii after setting its radius to the largest non-overlapping value.

backlog.spec: After the first SLSQP run, keep the best packing and repeatedly perturb it: add Gaussian noise (sigma about 0.02) to all centres and radii, clip centres into the square, re-run SLSQP from that point, and accept the result only if its repaired radius sum improves. Continue until the time budget is used. Use rng from the seed for every perturbation.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Starting from the best packing, remove the circle with the smallest radius, sample about 2000 random candidate points in the square, place the circle at the candidate whose distance to the nearest other circle minus its radius is largest, then re-run SLSQP on the full set. Accept if the repaired sum improves, otherwise keep the previous best.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Pass a jac argument to minimize that returns the exact gradient of the objective and of the constraint vector (pair distance terms, wall terms and radius non-negativity). Build the sparse pair Jacobian with the same index arrays iu used by cons. This removes finite-difference cost so each SLSQP iteration is much cheaper, which yields more restarts in the time budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Only include pair constraints for pairs whose centre distance is below a cutoff (for example the sum of current radii plus 0.15) when the problem is set up, rebuilding the list after each SLSQP call. Full pair sets are O(n^2) constraints of which most are slack. Keep the wall and non-negativity constraints for all circles. Verify the final repaired packing still checks every pair.
backlog.title: Neighbour-list pair constraints

backlog.spec: Phase 1: minimise a quadratic overlap penalty sum(max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2) plus wall penalties minus lambda times the radius sum with L-BFGS-B, increasing lambda geometrically over about 5 stages. Phase 2: feed the resulting centres and radii into the existing SLSQP call as the starting point. The penalty stage gives a feasible-ish start that SLSQP can polish quickly.
backlog.title: Penalty continuation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: After SLSQP and clipping, freeze the centres and solve a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog that maximises the sum of radii subject to linearised non-overlap constraints r_i + r_j <= d_ij (using current distances) and wall bounds r_i <= the distance to each wall. Iterate the LP a few times, re-linearising at the new centres, then apply the existing repair. This replaces the crude shrink step with an optimal radius assignment.
backlog.title: LP polish of radii with fixed centres

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP call with scipy.optimize.minimize using method trust-constr, passing the same objective and the NonlinearConstraint with lower bound 0 and upper bound infinity built from cons. Keep the time check and repair unchanged. Compare the best repaired sum against the SLSQP version within the same time budget and keep whichever construction is used consistently.
backlog.title: trust-constr instead of SLSQP

backlog.spec: Maintain an elite pool of the best 5 packings found so far, deduplicated by sorted radii. Each new start is either a fresh random init (probability 0.3) or a child made by taking the centres of one elite parent for the circles in one half of the square and the centres of another parent for the other half, then fixing the circle count by moving surplus circles to random positions. Run SLSQP on each child and insert the result into the pool.
backlog.title: Elite memetic recombination

backlog.spec: With probability 0.5 per restart, generate an initial configuration that is symmetric about the vertical line x = 0.5 or the diagonal: sample ceil(n/2) centres in one half, mirror them to fill the rest, and drop the extra circle at a random point if n is odd. Start SLSQP from that configuration. Mix these with the existing uniform random inits and keep the best result overall.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric initialisation

backlog.spec: Generate starts from a perturbed square or hexagonal lattice: choose a random lattice orientation near 0 or 30 degrees and random spacing so that about n points fall in the unit square, select n points, add uniform jitter of size 0.03 and clip into [0.05, 0.95]. Use these as the x0 centres with radii set to 0.05, alongside the existing uniform random inits.
backlog.title: Lattice-perturbed initialisation

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform draw of initial centres with a Latin hypercube sample in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2: split each axis into n equal strata, permute strata independently for x and y using rng, and draw one point per stratum cell. This spreads the starting circles more evenly, which usually gives SLSQP better-separated starts and fewer early collisions.
backlog.title: Latin hypercube centre sampling

backlog.spec: Change INIT_LOW from 0.1 to 0.0 so the initial centres range over the whole unit square, and sample radii uniformly in [0.01, 0.1] rather than fixing them at 0.05. Wider starts explore more of the configuration space across restarts. The clipping and repair steps already keep the final packing valid.
backlog.title: Widen the init box to the full square

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.93 so that the restart loop uses most of the 30 s CPU budget. The process_time check still stops the loop before the 45 s hard limit because the final repair takes only milliseconds. Leave all other logic unchanged so the gain comes purely from additional restarts.
backlog.title: Use more of the time budget

backlog.spec: Run the first few restarts with MAX_ITER set to 100 to rank starts cheaply, then re-run only the top 3 candidates with MAX_ITER set to 1000 and a tighter ftol of 1e-12. This spends the expensive long optimisation only on promising basins while keeping broad early exploration.
backlog.title: Adaptive SLSQP iteration cap

backlog.spec: Inside a basin-hopping loop started from the best packing, scale the perturbation sigma geometrically from 0.05 down to 0.002 over the remaining time budget, so early moves explore widely and late moves refine locally. Accept a new packing when its repaired radius sum is larger than the current one, and track the global best separately.
backlog.title: Annealed basin-hopping noise

backlog.spec: Phase 1: run SLSQP with all radii tied to a single shared variable t, maximising t subject to the packing constraints, which gives a well-spread equal-circle arrangement. Phase 2: release the radii to independent variables and run the existing SLSQP call from that state. The equal-radius phase avoids the poor local optima that independent radii often fall into early.
backlog.title: Two-phase equal-radius start

backlog.spec: Optimise the weighted objective minus sum of w_i r_i, where w_i starts at 1 plus a random perturbation and is annealed toward 1 over two SLSQP calls. The weights bias the early optimisation toward different size distributions, after which the true unweighted sum objective is restored for the final polish. Keep the final repair and best-tracking unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted objective annealing

backlog.spec: Replace the iterative max-overlap shrink in _repair with a single global scaling step: compute the minimum over all pairs of d_ij divided by (r_i + r_j) and the minimum wall margin ratio, scale all radii by the smaller of these ratios, then subtract SHRINK. This keeps the relative radius profile found by SLSQP instead of shrinking only the worst pair, and it is simpler to reason about.
backlog.title: Exact overlap-resolving repair

backlog.spec: From the best packing, pick two circles whose radii differ by more than 0.05 and swap their radii while keeping their centres, then re-run SLSQP from that state. Repeat with random pairs for a fixed number of attempts per restart. Swapping radii changes which positions host large circles, a move that random perturbation rarely produces.
backlog.title: Swap radii of mismatched circles

backlog.spec: Solve the problem for n minus 1 circles with a short SLSQP run, then insert the new circle at the largest empty spot found by sampling 2000 candidate points, set its radius to the largest feasible value at that point, and re-run SLSQP for n circles. Use this grown start in addition to random restarts, keeping whichever final packing has the largest repaired radius sum.
backlog.title: Grow from a smaller packing

backlog.spec: Add a small term -lambda * sum over pairs of log(d_ij) (with lambda about 1e-3) to the SLSQP objective during the first SLSQP call only, which discourages circles from collapsing together and pushes the start toward a well-spread configuration. Drop the term for the final polish so the reported objective is the true radius sum.
backlog.title: Soft spread regulariser

backlog.spec: Add a penalty of -mu * sum(log(r_i + 1e-3)) to the objective with mu decaying from 1e-2 to 0 across the SLSQP iterations of a single call, which keeps small circles from vanishing too early and lets the optimiser move them. Finish with an unregularised SLSQP call so the returned radii are optimal for the true objective.
backlog.title: Radius floor regularisation

backlog.spec: Generate a batch of 200 random starts at once, score each with a cheap feasibility-based estimate (for example the sum of radii obtained from the nearest-neighbour bound min(wall distance, half the nearest centre distance) using numpy broadcasting), and run full SLSQP only on the top 10 percent. This spends the expensive optimisation on the most promising starts without changing the optimiser.
backlog.title: Vectorised pre-screening of starts

backlog.spec: From the best packing, choose a random subset of about 12 circles that are spatially close to a random point, freeze all others, and run SLSQP only over the chosen subset with the frozen circles as fixed obstacles. Accept the result if the full repaired radius sum improves. Repeat with new random subsets for the time budget. Smaller subproblems solve faster and explore local rearrangements.
backlog.title: Random subset re-optimisation

backlog.spec: Start SLSQP with the wall constraints tightened so that circles must lie within [0.02, 0.98] squared, then relax the margin to zero in a second SLSQP call from the first result. The tightened stage keeps circles away from edges while the packing arranges itself, and the relaxed stage lets edge circles grow to their final size.
backlog.title: Gradual wall-margin relaxation

backlog.spec: Optimise under a prescribed symmetry, then unfold. Pick one symmetry at random per call from {reflection in the diagonal x=y, 180-degree rotation about (0.5,0.5)}, seeded by rng. Parameterise only ceil(n/2) free circles plus their images, with the self-symmetric circles (on the axis or centre) handled by fixing them to the symmetry set. Run SLSQP on the reduced variables (about half the constraints), which is much faster and explores a different region. Then unfold to all n circles, run one unconstrained SLSQP polish from that configuration, and keep the best of the symmetric and polished results in the basin-hopping loop.
backlog.title: Symmetry-reduced search

backlog.spec: Replace the random SLSQP start with an event-free compression. Start with n points at random positions with tiny radii. Repeat: grow every radius by a factor (1 + g), then push overlapping pairs and wall-violating circles apart with a few vectorised gradient steps on the squared overlap energy, using a shrinking step. When overlap energy cannot be driven to near zero, reduce g by half and add a small random jitter to centres. Stop when g falls below 1e-6. Use the resulting jammed packing as the start for the existing SLSQP and basin-hopping stages. Everything is numpy, with the seed controlling all randomness.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger-style growth compression

backlog.spec: Initialise centres with best-candidate (Mitchell) Poisson-disk sampling instead of uniform random points. For each new centre, draw k=30 candidates uniformly in [0,1]^2 and keep the one farthest from all existing centres. Use this for the first SLSQP start in _solve_once, with radii set to the distance to the nearest centre or wall times 0.5. Leave the basin-hopping stage unchanged. This gives evenly spread starts that avoid the clustered configurations uniform sampling produces.
backlog.title: Blue-noise Poisson-disk initialisation

backlog.spec: Build a start by placing circles one at a time in decreasing order of target radius, where the target radii follow a random decreasing profile drawn from rng. For each circle, find the point in a 200x200 grid that maximises the distance to existing centres and walls (the largest empty hole), place the circle there with radius equal to the minimum of that clearance and its target, and continue. Feed the resulting centres and radii as x0 to SLSQP. This replaces the uniform random start only, and costs well under a second for n=32.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-hole sequential placement

backlog.spec: Run K=4 basin-hopping chains in lockstep, each at a different temperature T in a geometric ladder from 0.0005 to 0.01. Each chain proposes a perturbed, SLSQP-relaxed, repaired packing and accepts it with the Metropolis rule on the sum of radii (accept if the new sum is larger, otherwise with probability exp(delta/T)). After each sweep, attempt swaps between neighbouring temperatures with the standard replica-exchange probability. Return the best packing seen by any chain. Keep the time budget and the perturbation scale unchanged.
backlog.title: Replica-exchange basin hopping

backlog.spec: Remove the radius variables from the optimisation. Define each radius as a function of the centres: r_i = softmin over the wall distances and the half-gaps (d_ij - r_j) with a temperature beta, using log-sum-exp with beta annealed from 30 to 300. Maximise the sum of these radii with L-BFGS-B on the 2n centre coordinates, using a numerical or analytic gradient. Finish with the existing SLSQP call starting from the resulting centres and radii. This cuts the variable count from 3n to 2n and removes the pairwise constraint matrix from the early stages.
backlog.title: Smooth-min radius reparameterisation

backlog.spec: Add a barrier term to the objective during the SLSQP stage in place of the hard overlap constraints alone. The objective becomes minus the sum of radii minus mu times the sum of log(slack) over all pair and wall slacks, with mu annealed from 1e-2 to 1e-6 across the stage. Each log term is evaluated only where the slack is positive, and a large penalty is used otherwise. Perform one final SLSQP solve with the hard constraints and mu=0, starting from the barrier solution. This keeps circles away from degenerate touching configurations early on and should reduce the amount the repair step has to shrink.
backlog.title: Log-barrier contact regularisation

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, identify rattlers: circles with fewer than two active contacts (pair or wall, within 1e-7 of zero slack). Remove the smallest rattler, search a 200x200 grid for the point with the largest clearance to other centres and walls, and move that circle there with radius set to the clearance. Re-run SLSQP from this configuration. Apply this move only with probability 0.3 inside the basin-hopping loop, so the step remains a targeted rearrangement rather than a full restart.
backlog.title: Rattler reinsertion into the largest hole

backlog.spec: Generate starts by solving a larger problem. Call _solve_once with n+1 circles from the random start, then delete the circle with the smallest radius and re-optimise the remaining n circles from the resulting centres and radii with SLSQP. Use this as a new start source with probability 0.5 at each restart, and keep the existing basin-hopping loop for the rest of the time. The idea is that a dense packing of n+1 circles sheds a circle into a configuration that is a good start for n.
backlog.title: Shrink from n+1 circles

backlog.spec: Allocate the time budget across many starts in rounds. Round 1 draws 40 random starts and runs SLSQP with maxiter=25 on each, keeping the top 10 by sum of repaired radii. Round 2 runs maxiter=80 on the top 10 and keeps the top 3. Round 3 gives the top 3 the full MAX_ITER budget and then uses the remaining time for basin hopping from the best. Stop each stage by the process-time clock so the total stays within TIME_FRACTION. This replaces the fixed-budget random restarts with a bracket that spends most compute on promising basins.
backlog.title: Successive-halving over starts

backlog.spec: Keep the basin-hopping loop, but count consecutive steps without improvement of best. If the count reaches K=25 (sum of radii not improved by more than 1e-6), discard the incumbent and restart from a fresh random SLSQP solve from _solve_once(n, rng), storing it as the new incumbent only if it is better than the old best. Otherwise continue basin hopping from the current best. Reset the counter after any restart or improvement. Use the same time check and repair step as now.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered fresh restart

backlog.spec: Replace the greedy accept rule (accept only if r.sum() > best sum) with threshold accepting. Maintain a current solution cur separate from the global best. Accept a candidate into cur if its repaired sum is greater than cur's sum minus a threshold T, where T decreases linearly from 0.01 at the start of the loop to 0 at the time limit, measured by elapsed process time over TIME_FRACTION*time_limit. Always update the global best when a candidate beats it. Perturbation and SLSQP solve stay as they are.
backlog.title: Threshold-accepting basin hopping

backlog.spec: In each basin-hopping step, add a quadratic proximal penalty to the SLSQP objective: minimise -sum(r) + lam * ||c - c0||^2 + lam * ||r - r0||^2, where c0, r0 are the perturbed start and lam = 0.5. This keeps each local solve near its starting basin rather than letting it drift to a distant one. Use the same constraints. After this solve, run one unpenalised SLSQP pass starting from the penalised result (maxiter MAX_ITER) to recover the true optimum, then repair as before.
backlog.title: Proximal-anchored SLSQP in basin hopping

backlog.spec: For each SLSQP solve in the basin-hopping loop, draw a random margin m uniformly in [0, 0.003] and tighten all non-overlap constraints to d_ij - r_i - r_j - m >= 0 and all wall constraints to margin m as well. The tightened problem pushes the optimiser into interior configurations with slack, which can escape jammed states. Run the final SLSQP pass with m=0 from that result so the returned solution satisfies the true constraints. Use the seed-driven rng for m.
backlog.title: Randomised constraint tightening during SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a small regularisation term to the SLSQP objective: minus sum(r) minus eps * sum(r*(1-r)) where eps = 1e-3 is fixed, or alternatively a term that penalises the variance of radii with weight 1e-3. The aim is to favour configurations where radii are not all equal, so the search explores more varied size distributions. After the regularised solve, run a plain SLSQP pass with the true objective (no regularisation) from its output and keep whichever packing has the larger true radius sum after repair.
backlog.title: Small-radius diversity bonus

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP initial solve with a hard-disk Monte Carlo compression. Start with n random centres and radii 0.001. Repeat for 2000 sweeps: propose a random displacement of each centre by a Gaussian step of size 0.05 times the current step scale, accept only if the circle stays inside the square and does not overlap any other circle given current radii, then try to grow each radius to the maximum allowed by its nearest neighbours and the walls, times 0.999 plus a small random factor. Reduce the step scale by a factor 0.99 every 50 sweeps. Pass the resulting centres and radii into SLSQP as the start. All randomness uses rng.
backlog.title: Hard-disk Monte Carlo compression start

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centres in _solve_once with a ring-shell layout. Place roughly 4 sqrt(n) circles evenly on the boundary perimeter inset by about 0.05, with an angular offset drawn from rng. Fill the remaining circles uniformly at random in the interior [0.15, 0.85]^2. Start radii at INIT_RADIUS. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. Use rng for all draws so that the seed controls the layout.
backlog.title: Ring-shell initialisation

backlog.spec: Add a move type to basin hopping. With probability 0.5, split the square into four quadrants around a random point (cx, cy) drawn in [0.35, 0.65]^2. Pick one quadrant at random. Take the circles whose centres lie inside it and solve a sub-problem with SLSQP on just those circles, keeping the other circles fixed as obstacles (add their non-overlap constraints as constants in the constraint function). Accept the sub-solution into the full configuration if the total radius sum improves after repair. Otherwise fall back to the existing full-SLSQP perturbation step.
backlog.title: Quadrant domain-decomposition moves

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP solve, run a short augmented Lagrangian loop. Use L-BFGS-B on the bounded variables (centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]) to minimise -sum(r) plus, for every constraint g_k >= 0 (pair overlaps and wall margins), the term (mu/2) * (max(0, lam_k - mu*g_k))^2 - lam_k^2/(2 mu), with lam_k as multipliers. After each inner solve, update lam_k = max(0, lam_k - mu*g_k) and increase mu by 2 for up to 5 outer iterations. Pass the output to the existing SLSQP solve as the starting point. This replaces the fixed-weight penalty idea by using multiplier updates.
backlog.title: Augmented-Lagrangian pre-solve with L-BFGS-B

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform Gaussian perturbation in basin hopping with a targeted one. Compute the contact graph of the incumbent: circles i and j are in contact if their gap is below 1e-4, and wall contact if a circle touches a wall within 1e-4. Identify rattlers as circles with fewer than 2 contacts. With probability 0.5, perturb only the rattlers and their neighbours with sigma 0.05, leaving the rest of the configuration fixed. Otherwise use the existing global Gaussian perturbation. Keep all other steps and the acceptance rule unchanged.
backlog.title: Contact-graph-guided perturbation

backlog.spec: Inside solve, for the first ~25% of the time budget, split the n circles into two groups (sizes n//2 and n - n//2). Run _solve_once independently on each group inside its own sub-square: a unit square scaled to half width, placed left and right (or top and bottom, chosen randomly from rng). Map the two sub-packings back to the unit square, scale radii by the same factor, and run _solve_once on the full set starting from the concatenated result with radii clipped to the walls. Use this merged solution as the initial incumbent for the existing basin-hopping loop. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Two-cluster hierarchical merge

backlog.spec: Replace the global Gaussian perturbation in the basin-hopping loop with a local one. With probability 0.5 each step, pick a random circle, take its k=4 nearest neighbours (by centre distance), and redraw only those five centres uniformly inside the square, keeping their radii shrunk by 0.5. Otherwise use the existing global perturbation. Feed the result to _solve_once with the same repair. Accept the move only if the repaired radius sum improves on the incumbent, as before.
backlog.title: Local cluster shake move

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when x0 is None, draw centres not uniformly but by rejection sampling against a density that is low near existing centres. For each new centre, draw 30 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 and keep the one whose distance to the nearest already-placed centre is largest (a best-candidate step). This is a cheap spread-out start. Keep the radii initialised at INIT_RADIUS and leave the SLSQP call and repair unchanged. Use only the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Density-matched rejection initialisation

backlog.spec: Track the success rate of basin-hopping steps over a sliding window of 20 steps. Start the Gaussian perturbation sigma at 0.02. Every 20 steps, multiply sigma by 1.2 if more than 1/5 of the steps improved the incumbent, and by 0.85 otherwise. Clamp sigma to [0.001, 0.1]. Apply the same sigma to both centre and radius noise. This replaces any fixed noise scale and needs no time-based schedule.
backlog.title: One-fifth-rule adaptive perturbation size

backlog.spec: After the final incumbent is chosen, identify the active contacts: pairs whose gap is below 1e-7 and walls where a circle touches the boundary within 1e-7. Form the system of equalities for these active constraints in the variables (centres, radii). Solve it with a few Gauss-Newton steps (least-squares via numpy.linalg.lstsq on the Jacobian of the active constraints) starting from the incumbent, keeping only steps that increase the radius sum and leave all non-active constraints satisfied. Finish with _repair so the packing is valid to 1e-10. Skip the polish if the system is rank-deficient or no step improves the sum.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish

backlog.spec: Maintain a running mean of the successful perturbation vectors in basin hopping. When a step improves the incumbent, add its perturbation delta to an exponentially weighted average (weight 0.2) and use this averaged direction, normalised and scaled by sigma, as the mean shift for the next proposals. Mix it with isotropic noise: proposal = incumbent + sigma * (0.5 * unit_mean_dir + 0.5 * gaussian). Keep sigma fixed at 0.02. The idea is to take larger steps along directions that have recently helped. Use only the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Learned perturbation direction (CMA-style)

backlog.spec: During each SLSQP call inside the basin-hopping loop, replace the objective -sum(r) with -sum(w_i * r_i), where the weights w_i are drawn once per call from uniform[0.9, 1.1] using the seeded rng. This breaks symmetry between circles and lets SLSQP reach different vertices of the feasible set. Constraints are unchanged. Score every candidate with the true unweighted radius sum after _repair, and keep the usual acceptance rule. Keep the first start unweighted.
backlog.title: Random per-circle objective weight jitter

backlog.spec: Each basin-hopping step, solve the packing in a container of side s drawn uniformly from [0.97, 1.03] instead of 1, by changing the wall constraints in _solve_once to use s. Rescale the resulting centres by 1/s so they fit the unit square, rescale radii by 1/s, then clip centres to [0, 1] and run _repair. Accept by the usual rule. The perturbation nudges the solution across the wall boundary and may move circles into new contact patterns. Use only the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Container scale jitter

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP solve in the basin-hopping loop, pick the circle with the smallest radius and try 30 random new centres for it, uniform in the square. For each trial, compute the local score: the sum of radii of that circle and its neighbours, after setting its radius to the largest value that fits without overlap with the rest of the packing (use the min of wall distance and gap to the nearest circle). Keep the best trial, then run _solve_once starting from that configuration. This makes a targeted move and avoids a fully random restart of the circle.
backlog.title: Greedy relocation sweep with local evaluation

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when x0 is None, generate the 2n centre coordinates from a Halton sequence in base 2 and base 3 (two dimensions) instead of rng.uniform. Use a random integer offset drawn from rng so each seed gives a different subsequence, then scale the points to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Keep the radii at INIT_RADIUS and leave everything else unchanged. Halton points cover the square more evenly than pseudo-random ones, which may give better basins for the first start.
backlog.title: Quasi-random Halton centre initialisation

backlog.spec: Inside the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.3 per step, pick a random circle that touches a wall (within 1e-6 of an edge). Slide its centre along that wall to a uniform random position on the wall, keeping its radius, and then run the existing relocate-free SLSQP solve on the result. Otherwise keep the current perturbation. This is one extra branch in the loop and uses only numpy.
backlog.title: Wall-slide move in basin hopping

backlog.spec: For each basin-hopping step, run a cheap SLSQP with maxiter 25 from the perturbed start and compute its repaired sum of radii. Only if that screened sum is within 0.01 of the incumbent's sum, run the full SLSQP with MAX_ITER 200 from the same start and accept it if it improves the incumbent. This spends the 30 s budget on more candidates, with the expensive solve reserved for plausible ones.
backlog.title: Two-stage screening of basin-hopping candidates

backlog.spec: Change the pair constraint to d_ij - r_i - r_j - MARGIN >= 0 with MARGIN = 1e-7, and the wall constraints to use the same margin. SLSQP's tolerance then tends to land slightly inside the feasible set, so _repair shrinks less and the repaired sum keeps more of the optimiser's value. Keep SHRINK at 1e-9 and check the harness tolerance is still met.
backlog.title: Feasibility margin in the SLSQP pair constraints

backlog.spec: Remove the four wall-constraint blocks from cons() (the x-r, y-r, 1-x-r, 1-y-r terms) and pass the box limits through SLSQP's bounds argument: centres in [0, 1] and radii in [0, 0.5]. Keep the r >= 0 and pair constraints as they are. This shrinks the constraint matrix by about 4n rows, which should give SLSQP more iterations within the time limit.
backlog.title: Native box bounds instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: In each basin-hopping step, take the 25 percent largest-radius circles of the incumbent and hold their centres fixed while the rest are perturbed and solved with SLSQP, using a reduced problem over the other circles with the fixed ones included as constants in the pair constraints. Then run one full SLSQP over all circles from that result, accepting it only if its repaired sum improves the incumbent. This focuses the search on the loose part of the packing.
backlog.title: Frozen-core perturbation stage

backlog.spec: Each basin-hopping step, choose a random point p in the square and a radius R uniformly between 0.2 and 0.35. Rotate the centres of all circles within distance R of p about p by a random angle in [-pi/3, pi/3], keep only rotated centres inside the square (clip them), and then run the usual SLSQP. This is a larger structured move than Gaussian noise and can reorder a local region of the packing.
backlog.title: Sub-disk rotation kick

backlog.spec: When comparing a candidate with the incumbent, accept it when its repaired sum is larger, or when the sums differ by less than 1e-5 and its smallest radius is larger. This lexicographic rule lets the search move along flat directions of the sum toward packings with more evenly sized circles, which can open room for later improvements. It changes only the acceptance comparison.
backlog.title: Secondary max-min radius tie-break

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random first-start centres in _solve_once with a quasi-random Halton sequence of 2n points in [0.05, 0.95]^2, scrambled by a random shift taken from the seed, and place the first four centres at the corners (0.05, 0.05), (0.95, 0.05), (0.05, 0.95), (0.95, 0.95). Initial radii stay at INIT_RADIUS. Only the start changes; the rest of the pipeline stays the same.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored initial layout with Halton centres

backlog.spec: Track the number of basin-hopping steps since the incumbent last improved. If that count exceeds 40, replace the chain's current solution with a fresh random SLSQP start, keep the global best as it is, and reset the counter. The global best is only replaced when a candidate beats it. This gives the search a diversified restart when it stalls, without discarding the best packing found.
backlog.title: Reheated restart after stagnation

backlog.spec: Within _relocate, weight the smallest circle's candidate score by the number of contacts it would make, counting a contact as a neighbour within 1e-3 of touching, and add a bonus of 0.5 times that count to the score. Draw the candidate centre from a random point that lies in the largest empty region found from 200 uniform samples, using the existing trials loop. This favours moves that place the smallest circle where it wedges between existing ones.
backlog.title: Rattler-aware relocation weights

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP call inside _solve_once with a sequential linear programming loop. At each iterate (c, r), linearise every pair-distance constraint, the wall constraints and the radius bounds, then solve the LP max sum(dr) using scipy.optimize.linprog(method='highs') over the step (dc, dr) with box trust-region bounds |dc|, |dr| <= delta. Accept the step if the true constraint violation shrinks and the objective rises, otherwise halve delta. Stop when delta < 1e-7 or after 60 iterations. Restrict the pair constraints to pairs closer than 2*(r_i+r_j)+0.1 to keep the LP small. The LP vertex solutions should land exactly on the active contacts, which SLSQP often leaves slightly loose. Keep the basin-hopping loop and _repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Sequential LP trust-region polish

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping step, instead of isotropic Gaussian noise on the incumbent, build the Hessian of a penalty energy E(c,r) = -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, overlap)^2 + max(0, wall violation)^2) at the incumbent, using finite differences of the analytic gradient or a numerical Hessian (dimension 3n = 96, cheap). Take the eigenvectors with the 5 smallest non-zero eigenvalues (the floppy modes) and displace the incumbent along a random combination of them with amplitude drawn from U[0.01, 0.05], then clip to the square. Use the Gaussian kick with probability 0.5 and this soft-mode kick otherwise. Pass the perturbed point to _solve_once as the warm start, with everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Soft-mode Hessian perturbation kick

backlog.spec: Replace the random multi-start with a population-based search. Keep a population of 40 candidate packings encoded as 3n-vectors (centres plus radii). Each generation, form a trial vector with DE/rand/1/bin (F=0.6, CR=0.9) and score it by a penalised objective: sum of radii after the greedy repair of _repair. Keep the top 8 members after each generation and polish only the best candidate with _solve_once as a warm start. Loop until 80 percent of the CPU budget is used, then return the best polished packing. Vectorise the repair and scoring over the population where possible so that a generation takes well under 0.1 s for n=32.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over centres with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Define four basin-hopping moves: Gaussian kick (sigma 0.02), relocate-smallest (existing _relocate), a local cluster shake of five neighbouring circles, and a wall-slide that moves one boundary circle along its wall by U[-0.1,0.1]. Keep a success score per move, initialised at 1. Choose the move each step with probability proportional to its score plus 0.2 as an exploration floor. After each step, add 1 to the score of the move if it improved the incumbent and multiply all scores by 0.99 to forget old results. Log nothing and keep the code under 25 added lines.
backlog.title: Adaptive operator selection over perturbation moves

backlog.spec: Add a new perturbation applied before the SLSQP solve in the basin-hopping loop. Sample 4000 random points in the unit square and assign each to the nearest centre under the power (radically weighted) distance d(p,c_i)^2 - r_i^2. Move each centre to the centroid of its assigned points, blended with its current position at weight 0.5, for 3 iterations. This pushes the packing toward a power-diagram centroidal state and removes local bias before the SLSQP solve. Apply this move with probability 0.3 per step, otherwise use the existing kick. Seed the sampling from the rng argument.
backlog.title: Lloyd centroidal relaxation kick

backlog.spec: Modify _relocate so it avoids moving circles that were relocated in the last 5 basin-hopping steps. Maintain a deque of recently moved indices and exclude them from the candidate set when choosing k = argmin(r). If all small circles are tabu, pick the smallest non-tabu circle instead. Also, when a step is rejected (the new packing does not beat the incumbent), record the moved index in the tabu list anyway so the search keeps cycling through different circles. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Tabu-protected relocation

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping kick, scale the Gaussian noise per circle by its contact count instead of using a uniform sigma. Compute contacts from the incumbent as pairs with centre distance less than r_i + r_j + 1e-3, plus wall contacts where any side is within 1e-3 of the wall. Set sigma_i = 0.03 for circles with 0 or 1 contacts (likely rattlers, which should move freely) and sigma_i = 0.01 for circles with 4 or more contacts (rigid core, which should move little). Use 0.02 otherwise. Apply the same per-circle sigma to the radius noise. Everything else in the loop stays the same.
backlog.title: Contact-count-scaled perturbation noise

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP multi-start, run scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on the penalised energy E(c,r) = -sum(r) + mu * (sum of squared pair overlaps + squared wall violations), with mu = 100, over bounds [0,1] for centres and [0,0.5] for radii. Pass the rng-derived seed as seed and set maxfun so the call uses about 25 percent of the CPU budget. Use the best point as the warm start for _solve_once and then continue with the basin hopping loop unchanged. This tests whether a global annealer finds a better basin than random starts for n=32.
backlog.title: Dual annealing global search on penalty energy

backlog.spec: Add a topology move to the basin-hopping step with probability 0.2. Choose a random pair of circles whose centres are within 2.5 times the mean radius of each other, delete both, and insert one circle at their midpoint with radius equal to the sum of their radii times 0.8 (clipped to the wall limits). Then reinsert a circle at the centre of the largest empty region found by sampling 500 random points, with radius equal to the distance to the nearest circle or wall. Run SLSQP on the modified packing, which has n circles again, and accept it only if the repaired sum of radii beats the incumbent.
backlog.title: Merge-and-split topology move

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP polish in the basin-hopping loop, run a short coordinate pattern search on the repaired packing. For 40 iterations, pick a random circle and a random axis, try moving that centre coordinate by +step and -step with step starting at 0.01 and halving on failure, and accept a move only if _repair of the new packing has a larger sum of radii. Stop early when step < 1e-4. This is derivative-free and only accepts strict improvements, so it cannot reduce the score. It targets the small residual gap between the SLSQP optimum and the published 2.9370 value.
backlog.title: Pattern search over centre coordinates
